chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person in Ihram who squeezes a pimple and binds a bandage over an ulcer. He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِم: The person in the state of Ihram
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What medical treatments are permissible for a person in Ihram?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor medical interventions like squeezing a pustule or bandaging a wound do not break the state of Ihram, distinguishing them from prohibited acts like using scented oils. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*takhaffuf*) in ritual consecration, ensuring that necessary treatment for illness or injury does not impose undue hardship on the pilgrim.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam squeezing the pimple and bandage upon his ulcer. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who is in the state of Ihram; if he can squeeze a pimple or bandage a wound. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
